issues.description: Method calculateRemainingOrderNumber(): The problem statement (UML and textual specification) declares calculateRemainingOrderNumber() as returning an int (the number of remaining orders). The solution implementation (SealSaloon.java) defines calculateRemainingOrderNumber() with the signature `public void calculateRemainingOrderNumber()` and its body prints order numbers instead of returning an int. This mismatch between the specified return type (int) and the implemented return type (void) creates ambiguity for students about the intended API and can cause tests or templates that expect an int to fail or be confusing.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and implementation consistent. Either: (A) Change the problem statement (UML and text) to declare calculateRemainingOrderNumber() as void and document that it prints remaining order numbers (and update any tests and the UML accordingly), or (B) Change the implementation and template so calculateRemainingOrderNumber() returns an int (the remaining order count) and remove printing from the method (move printing to callers). Update the UML, the textual description, the template SealSaloon stub (if present), and any tests to match the chosen signature and behavior.
